heading: INT. PETALS & STEM FLORIST - COLD ROOM - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. PETALS & STEM FLORIST - COLD ROOM - AFTERNOON
A walk-in cooler, white and humming, banked with buckets of peonies, ranunculus, and dusty-blue hydrangeas.
The air smells of cut stems and cold iron.
Condensation beads the glass door.
ELEANOR WYNDHAM-ROSS, 60s, in a long apron, trims stems at a steel table with a hooked knife.
THEO BRANDVOLD, 20s, her assistant, ties ribbons with painstaking slowness.
MIRABEL SOUZA, 30s, a bride in a cardigan over her wedding dress, drifts from bucket to bucket, touching petals.
JUDE ASANTE, 30s, her groom, tucks a stray hair behind her ear.
Peonies don't love the cold.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: But they keep better.
units.name: THEO

units.text: Everything keeps better in the cold.
units.name: MIRABEL

units.text: Even us?
units.name: JUDE

units.text: Especially us.
units.name: MIRABEL

units.text: The door opens.
A WOMAN IN A YELLOW RAINCOAT, 40s, drips on the threshold.
She looks at the four of them, at the flowers, at the clock.
I'm sorry. I think I'm early.
units.name: WOMAN IN YELLOW

units.text: For what, dear?
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: My sister's wedding.
units.name: WOMAN IN YELLOW

units.text: That's us.
units.name: THEO

units.text: That's me. You're Seraphina?
units.name: MIRABEL

units.text: I took the wrong train.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: You look like Mama.
units.name: MIRABEL

units.text: Seraphina crosses the cold room in four steps.
They fold into one another, the flowers shivering around them.
